wine_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales
wrong_facts: Hook claims Hunter Valley has 'cool maritime influence' — Hunter Valley is actually warm and humid, not cool maritime; the Tasman Sea moderates but the region is classified as warm

Terroir section mentions 'volcanic basalt and black silty loam over alkaline clay' — this is not verified for Tyrrell's Short Flat vineyard and may be fabricated or confused with other Hunter sub-regions

Comparable wines section says Graves Blanc is 'Sauvignon Blanc-based' — Domaine de Chevalier Blanc and Château de Fieuzal Blanc are Sauvignon Blanc/Semillon blends, not purely Sauvignon Blanc-based (though Sauvignon often dominates)

Cellar recommendation says 'entering its sweet spot at five years old' for the 2015 — but the ground truth says Tyrrell's doesn't release until 5 years of age, so at release it's just beginning, not in its sweet spot
Value assessment mentions 'Tyrrell's Vat 101' as a comparable — Vat 101 is actually a Chardonnay, not a Semillon
fabricated_numbers: 15-20 years aging potential is a reasonable estimate but not in context data
50-55°F storage temperature is general wine knowledge, not fabricated per se
